label: The name of a profession or craft as an activity (acting, conducting, filmmaking, teaching, design, programming, bartending), esp. after 'for/in/of/at' where a skill or career would follow; fires on the word's stem token, covers a mix of occupations and disciplines

probed_before.source: this checkout's .probe-log, before the pre-registration commit

notes: 10x pilot (concept-maps/tenx, census arm): label and 16 sentences written by a fresh Sonnet 5.5 subagent from a packet (card + all-pole band samples + concept-census evidence (which concepts and domains selected the pole)); no probes. An Opus gate checked rule-level items only (8 + 8, 0 overlap with census and probe text, near misses free of the declared trigger) and edited nothing. Labeller's note: Top examples are all stems of occupation/craft gerunds (conducting, bartending, filmmaking, choreographing, teaching, acting, design); census shows 65% of profession items fire it versus ~0% of objects, and the output suppresses ' profession/skills/expertise'. Strong activations also include discipline names (engineering, photography, singing), so coverage is a mix of professions and disciplines.
